bottom_line: In TRILOGY ACS (age <75 years), prasugrel versus clopidogrel did not significantly reduce the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.05).
implications: These data show no statistically significant reduction in the primary composite end point with prasugrel versus clopidogrel in patients <75 years (HR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.05; P=0.21). The prespecified recurrent-event analysis supports a possible reduction in multiple recurrent ischemic events (HR 0.85; 95% CI, 0.72 to 1.00; P=0.04), while key severe/intracranial bleeding outcomes were reported as similar between groups and TIMI major bleeding was not significantly different (HR 1.31; 95% CI, 0.81 to 2.11).

major_points.text: Double-blind, randomized evaluation of long-term prasugrel vs clopidogrel in medically managed ACS without revascularization, in a primary analysis of patients <75 years.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, randomized trial, in a primary analysis involving 7243 patients under the age of 75 years receiving aspirin, we evaluated up to 30 months of treatment with prasugrel (10 mg daily) versus clopidogrel (75 mg daily).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke in patients under 75 years.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myo- cardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke among pa- tients under the age of 75 years.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint result at median follow-up 17 months: 13.9% vs 16.0%, HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.79–1.05), P=0.21.
major_points.quote: At a median follow-up of 17 months, the primary end point ... occurred in 13.9% of the prasugrel group and 16.0% of the clopidogrel group (hazard ratio in the prasugrel group, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.05; P = 0.21).

major_points.text: Prespecified recurrent-event analysis suggested lower risk with prasugrel in patients under 75 years (HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.72–1.00; P=0.04).
major_points.quote: The pre- specified analysis of multiple recurrent ischemic events (all components of the pri- mary end point) suggested a lower risk for prasugrel among patients under the age of 75 years (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.72 to 1.00; P = 0.04).

major_points.text: Severe and intracranial bleeding rates were similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Rates of severe and intra- cranial bleeding were similar in the two groups in all age groups.

major_points.text: Among <75 years, TIMI major bleeding was 2.1 vs 1.5 (HR 1.31; 95% CI 0.81–2.11; P=0.27).

criticisms.text: Post hoc time-dependent analysis was performed after observing divergence after 12 months.
criticisms.quote: we tested the difference in treatment effect between the first 12 months and subsequent months in a post hoc analysis using a time-dependent Cox proportional-hazards model

criticisms.quote: The reasons for this finding remain uncertain

criticisms.text: Median follow-up may not have been long enough to explore divergence of ischemic events in medically managed patients.
criticisms.quote: it is possible that a median follow-up period of 17 months was not long enough to explore the divergence of is­che­mic events in patients receiving medical therapy alone.

criticisms.text: In patients ≥75 years, the 5-mg prasugrel dose used had not been evaluated in previous outcomes trials.
criticisms.quote: The 5-mg dose that was used in participants 75 years of age or older had not been evaluated in previous out- comes trials.
